title: Privileged Knowledge State Distillation for Reinforcement Learning-based Educational Path Recommendation

problem.claim: Educational recommendation aims to suggest knowledge concepts matching a learner's ability to support personalized learning.

gap.claim: Existing reinforcement-learning approaches struggle to handle diverse and dynamic learner knowledge states.

contributions.claim: The PKSD framework uses actual knowledge states as privileged information during training to improve learner-adaptive recommendations.
PKSD distills the adaptation capability into a knowledge state adapter that estimates privileged knowledge states during inference.
GEPKSD incorporates graph structure learning for knowledge concepts into PKSD.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating PKSD and GEPKSD with five reinforcement-learning methods across four public simulators.
The authors report that PKSD consistently improves recommendation performance across the evaluated reinforcement-learning methods.
The authors report that GEPKSD further improves PKSD effectiveness in all simulations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Educational recommendation targets learner-appropriate knowledge concepts for personalized learning.
Reinforcement-learning methods encode exercise logs as learner states and use agents to make recommendations.
These methods have difficulty representing diverse and dynamic learner knowledge states.
PKSD uses privileged knowledge states during training, distills them into an adapter for inference, and GEPKSD adds concept graph structure learning.
The methods are evaluated with multiple reinforcement-learning methods and public simulators, with reported performance improvements.

source_observation.claim: Privileged information available during training can be distilled into an adapter for use when that information is unavailable at inference.

interpretation.claim: Training-time access to richer state information may improve deployment-time adaptation when the richer information cannot be observed.

application.claim: Consider privileged-state distillation for sequential decision systems that have richer supervision during training than during deployment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the evaluated educational recommendation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not name the five reinforcement-learning methods or four public simulators.
The abstract does not specify the knowledge state adapter or graph structure learning procedure.
